title: Clearday Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy
intro_html:
Effective date: [EFFECTIVE DATE]

Last updated: [EFFECTIVE DATE]

This policy explains how Mental Health Tools LLC ("we" or "us"), a New Jersey company, handles consumer health data in Clearday, our app for cutting back on or stopping substance use. Consumer health data means information linked to you that says something about your physical or mental health, past, present or future. This policy covers what Washington's My Health My Data Act (RCW 19.373) and Nevada's consumer health data law (NRS 603A.400 to 603A.550) require. Our Privacy Policy covers everything else.

sections.heading: Consumer health data we collect and how we use it
sections.html:
Because Clearday is about substance use, we treat all of the following as consumer health data.

  • Check-ins. Your mood, and for each substance a craving score (0 to 10) and how much you cut back (0 to 100%), plus an optional note and the date. We use them to show your progress, insights and weekly trends, and, if Reflections is on, to give it context.
  • Your plan. The substances you're working on (cannabis, alcohol, nicotine, vaping or stimulants), including any you've archived (paused), a weekly spending estimate for each, your day one (the day you started) and the reasons you chose or wrote down. An archived substance keeps its history so you can bring it back. We use them to build your plan, work out money saved, and remind you of your reasons, for example on the SOS screen, and, if Reflections is on, to give it context.
  • Skills, if-then plans and SOS. Which skills you practiced, how many times, and when you last practiced each, the skills you pinned, the if-then plans you saved, and a count of how many times you've used SOS. We use them to track your practice and keep your tools at hand. If Reflections is on, your pinned skills also give it context. The urge ratings you give during SOS stay on your phone.
  • Progress we calculate. Banked days, money saved, streaks, badges and weekly averages, worked out from your check-ins and plan. We use them to show your progress and, if Reflections is on, to give it context.
  • Reflections conversations. Reflections is Clearday's AI coach. If you turn it on, we store your messages and its replies, including the message it opens with each day and the homework it closes with, and we count how many sessions you've had. We keep your newest 400 messages, plus your latest opening and homework. We use them to run Reflections and give later sessions context. The app shows only today's session and its homework. Earlier messages stay on our server.
  • Reflections' private notes. When a session closes, the AI writes a short private note about what you shared, so later sessions can pick up where you left off. We keep your newest 120 notes. The notes are never shown in the app, but they're sent back to the AI in later sessions, and you can ask us for a copy.
  • Crisis-language flag. Our server automatically checks each Reflections message for words about suicide, self-harm or overdose. If a message matches, we tag it and its reply. We use the flag to show you crisis resources, to tell Reflections to respond with care (including later that day), and to keep Reflections open for you that day: a flagged message is never turned away because of the daily limit or an ended free trial, and the day gets a few extra turns. If more than 40 of your messages in one day match, Reflections answers the rest with a short fixed message instead of the AI, and our server log notes your internal account number once. This is a computer check, and no person is alerted.
  • Your account. Having a Clearday account could suggest something about your health, so we treat your account details as consumer health data too: your email address, your first name (at sign-up we fill in one guessed from your email address, and you can change it), your time zone, a scrambled (hashed) copy of your password, your sign-up date, whether you've confirmed your email, when you agreed to our Terms and allowed Reflections, when you last used Start over, and security records such as one-time codes (also scrambled). We use them to run your account and keep it secure, to work out your free trial, and to date each check-in by your own day. If Reflections is on, it also uses your first name.
  • Clearday Plus. Whether you have Clearday Plus, which option you bought (Monthly, Annual or Lifetime) and Apple's reference number for the purchase (its original transaction ID). We use them to unlock Clearday Plus.
  • Connection details. Like any server, ours sees your IP address and basic details about your app or browser with each request. Our host's server logs record these with the time and the web address requested, which shows which part of Clearday you used and when (for example, a check-in, SOS or Reflections). To block abuse, our server also holds IP addresses, and email addresses typed into failed sign-ins, in temporary memory until it restarts. We use them to run Clearday, keep it secure and fix problems.
  • Anything else you tell us. Health details you include in feedback you send in the app, or in emails to our support address. We use them to answer you and fix what you report.

sections.heading: Where it comes from
sections.html:
• You, when you set up your plan, check in, practice skills, use SOS, write in Reflections, or send us feedback or email.
  • The app and our server, which calculate your progress from what you enter, keep your account records and run the crisis-language check.
  • Anthropic's AI, only if you turn Reflections on. It writes Reflections' replies, homework and private notes.
  • Your phone, which tells us its time zone so each check-in is dated by your own day (it starts at 4am where you are), and which sends your IP address and app details with each request.
  • Apple, through the App Store on your phone, which tells the app which Clearday Plus option you bought and its reference number.

sections.heading: Why we collect, use and share it
sections.html:
We collect, use and share consumer health data only to:

  • Give you the Clearday features you use: check-ins, your plan, progress, skills, if-then plans and SOS.
  • Run Reflections, if you turn it on, including sending information to Anthropic so it can write replies.
  • Show you crisis resources, and keep Reflections open for you, when a Reflections message matches the crisis-language check.
  • Run your account and Clearday Plus.
  • Keep Clearday secure and working, and fix problems.
  • Answer your messages and requests, including the requests described below.
  • Meet our legal duties.

We never use it for advertising or marketing, never sell it, and never use it to train AI.

sections.heading: What we share, and with whom
sections.html:
Nevada's law calls giving information to Anthropic or to our service providers "sharing", so we list every one of them here.

Anthropic, only with your permission

Reflections uses AI from Anthropic, PBC. Nothing goes to Anthropic unless you tap Allow (or Allow and start) on the permission screen. That screen appears before your first reflection, any time you start Reflections while it's off, and when you turn on Use AI for Reflections in You › Privacy & data.

Once a day when you open Reflections (for its opening message), and each time you send it a message, our server (never your phone) sends Anthropic:

  • Your messages and recent Reflections conversations (up to the last 24 messages, yours and the AI's, which can go back to earlier days)
  • Your first name (if you haven't changed it, the one we guessed from your email address)
  • The substances you're working on, with banked days and this week's average craving and reduction for each, your total banked days and money saved, and whether you've checked in today
  • Your reasons and pinned skills
  • Short excerpts (up to 160 characters each) from up to 6 of your recent check-in notes
  • Your last homework, up to 14 of Reflections' private notes, and how many sessions you've had
  • Whether your message, or anything earlier that day, matched the crisis-language check

We never send Anthropic your email address, password, internal account number, IP address, time zone, profile photo, subscription details, if-then plans, or your individual daily moods and scores. But your messages and note excerpts go as you wrote them, so any such details you type there go too.

Anthropic uses what it receives to write Reflections' replies and to check for misuse of its service. Anthropic's commercial terms don't allow it to train its AI on what we send.

Service providers that store or handle it for us

  • PythonAnywhere hosts our server and database in the United States, so it stores everything in our database: all the consumer health data listed above, except emails you send to our support address. It also keeps our server logs.
  • Microsoft (Microsoft 365) hosts our support mailbox, so it holds anything you email us.
  • Resend delivers account emails, such as confirmation codes and password-reset links. It gets your email address (which shows you have a Clearday account), in some emails a greeting name based on that address, and the one-time code or link. It gets nothing from your check-ins or Reflections. We don't use open or click tracking.

They handle it on our behalf, under contracts that limit what they can do with it. Each also uses its own subcontractors to run its service. For example, PythonAnywhere runs on Amazon Web Services computers in the United States.

Companies that keep their own records

  • Apple processes Clearday Plus purchases and keeps its own record of them in your Apple Account, under Apple's privacy policy.
  • GitHub hosts our website, mentalhealthtools.net, where this policy is published, and logs visitors' IP addresses for security under the GitHub Privacy Statement. It doesn't receive anything you enter in Clearday.

No one else

We have no affiliates, and we never sell consumer health data. We'll disclose it to anyone else only when the law requires it, such as for a valid court order.

If Mental Health Tools LLC is ever part of a merger or sale, your information may move to the new owner, who must keep the promises in this policy. We'll email you before it moves, so you can delete your account first, and any new use would still need your agreement, as described in Changes to this policy.

sections.heading: How we store and process it
sections.html:
• The app sends your information to our server over encrypted (HTTPS) connections. Our server stores it in our database at PythonAnywhere, in the United States. We keep no backups of our own.
  • Our server works out your progress and runs the crisis-language check automatically. With your permission, it sends Reflections requests to Anthropic, which stores data in the United States but may process requests in other countries.
  • The app keeps a copy of your account data on your phone so it opens offline. Logging out, Start over or deleting your account removes it from that phone. The app also keeps a short code made from your email address, so it remembers you've seen the free-trial screen. That code stays on the phone after you log out, and deleting your account on that phone removes it.
  • Authorized people at Mental Health Tools LLC can see a list of accounts. It shows each account's email address, name, sign-up date, whether setup is finished, subscription or trial status, days since day one and SOS count. They can also read the feedback you send, and they have access to the database to run the service. We look at your check-ins or Reflections conversations only when you ask us to, to fix a problem you reported, to keep the service secure, or when the law requires it.
  • Our host's server logs record your IP address, the time, the web address of each request (for links in our emails, that includes the one-time code) and app or browser details. The lines our own code writes to those logs never include what you write. If more than 40 of your Reflections messages in one day match the crisis-language check, the log records your internal account number once, but none of your messages.

sections.heading: Tracking across sites and apps
sections.html: Clearday and our websites have no advertising, analytics or tracking tools. Apart from Apple's own record of a Clearday Plus purchase and GitHub's security logs (see Companies that keep their own records), no other company collects consumer health data about you over time or across other websites or apps when you use Clearday or our websites.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.html:
See what we have (confirm and access)

You can ask whether we collect, share or sell consumer health data about you (we never sell it), and get a copy of it, including older Reflections messages and Reflections' private notes that the app doesn't show. We'll also give you a list of every company we've shared it with (including Anthropic and our service providers), with an email address or web page for contacting each one.

Take back permission, or stop collection

Turn off Use AI for Reflections in You › Privacy & data. It takes effect at once: nothing new is stored for Reflections or sent to Anthropic. It can't take back what Anthropic already received (Anthropic deletes it on the schedule under Delete, below). Your past Reflections stay until you use Start over, delete your account, or ask us by email to delete them.

The rest of Clearday collects information only while you use it. To stop that, stop using Clearday, or delete your account in the app or by emailing us.

Delete

  • Delete my account (You › Privacy & data, with your password) deletes your account and everything in it from our database right away, and the deleted data is overwritten in our database file. It also clears the offline copy and the free-trial code on that phone.
  • Start over (same screen) erases your check-ins, substances and spending estimates, reasons and day one, skill practice and pinned skills, if-then plans, SOS count, and Reflections conversations, private notes and session count. It keeps your account, name, time zone, Clearday Plus status, feedback and your Use AI for Reflections setting.
  • By email, you can ask us to delete all or part of your data. We'll do it within 30 days after we confirm the request is from you, and in any case within 45 days of receiving it (or within the extra time we've told you about).
  • Backups and logs. Our host, PythonAnywhere, may keep disaster-recovery copies of its servers, which can include our database, for up to 7 days, and we clear our server logs automatically at least every 30 days. After that, deleted data is gone from these copies too.
  • Copies held by others. Anthropic deletes what it received within 30 days. There's one exception: if Anthropic's own safety systems flag something as breaking its usage rules, Anthropic may keep that content for up to 2 years, and the safety ratings its systems gave it for up to 7 years. This is separate from Clearday's crisis-language check. Anthropic may also keep data longer when the law requires it. Resend keeps its email records for 30 days, and if an email to you bounces or you mark one as spam, it may keep your address on a do-not-send list. We delete support emails within 2 years, or sooner when you ask.

Review and change

In the app you can see your progress, change your name, reasons and pinned skills, add or archive substances, change your spending estimate while you're working on one substance, and redo a check-in for any day in the past week. To see or change anything else, email us. That includes changing your email address, a check-in older than a week, or a spending estimate when you're working on more than one substance, and deleting a single check-in or if-then plan.

sections.heading: How to use your rights
sections.html:
Use the tools in the app described above, or email support@mentalhealthtools.net from the email address on your Clearday account and tell us what you'd like us to do. It helps to put "Privacy request" in the subject. You'll also find this address in the app under You › Help & support. If you don't have a Clearday account (for example, you've only emailed us), email us from the address you used.

  • Confirming it's you. We may need to check that a request really comes from you, usually by replying to your account email address. You don't need to create an account. If you no longer have access to that address, email us from another one. We'll try to confirm it's you another way, and if we can't, we'll tell you why we can't act on the request.
  • When we act. We'll do what you asked, or tell you why we can't, within 45 days of receiving your request. If we need more time, we may extend that once, by up to 45 more days, and we'll tell you why within the first 45 days.
  • Cost. Requests are free, and your first two in any year always are. If requests are clearly unfounded, excessive or repetitive, we may charge a reasonable fee to cover our costs (or, for Washington requests, decline them), and we'll explain why.

sections.heading: If we say no: appeals
sections.html:
If we decline all or part of your request, you can appeal. Reply to our answer, or email support@mentalhealthtools.net, with "Appeal" in the subject. Within 45 days of receiving your appeal, we'll tell you in writing what we did or didn't do, and why.

If we deny your appeal, you can file a complaint with your state's attorney general, and our answer will tell you how to reach them:

  • Washington: File a complaint with the Washington Attorney General
  • Nevada: Nevada Attorney General complaints page

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
sections.html: If we make a material (important) change to this policy, we'll email you at the address on your account before it takes effect, and we'll update the dates at the top. We won't start collecting, using or sharing consumer health data in a new way, such as a new category, purpose or third party, unless we tell you first and you agree. The same goes for using information we already have in a materially different way.
